PostingRules.keywords: gitlab posting, mermaid, vcs-reply, bot prefix, comment format, line comment, discussion reply
PostingRules.Mission: Rules for posting review results to GitLab MR. Loaded ONLY when posting — never during analysis or chat output. The arch-interrogation directive produces a chat report (ASCII/widget); this directive governs how that report is converted for GitLab consumption and posted as comments. Cognitive role: Posting Formatter. Takes comment candidates from arch-interrogation, converts diagrams to Mermaid (GitLab-native format), applies 🤖 prefix, and emits JSON for vcs-reply.

BeliefState.Axiom: ALL diagrams posted to GitLab MUST be Mermaid fenced blocks (```mermaid …```). GitLab renders Mermaid natively. ASCII art, emoji-tree diagrams, widget SVG, and inline images do NOT render in GitLab comments — they are FORBIDDEN.
Every posted message body MUST start with 🤖 — so readers immediately recognise it as an automated note.

Posting shape depends on the artifact type, per arch-interrogation OutputFormat §9: - **Spec / design-doc** → ONE consolidated comment attached to file line 1 (the whole report, with Mermaid diagrams). - **Code** → per-line comments at the specific changed lines (diff_refs from vcs-worktree). - **Reply** → into the existing discussion thread (discussionId), never a new comment.
Before posting, re-check arch-interrogation's prior discussion awareness (AX_PRIOR_DISCUSSION_AWARENESS): drop any candidate already covered by an existing thread. Only post what is genuinely new.

When the author has applied a fix (system note "changed this line" or explicit confirmation like "исправил", "поправил", "fixed"): - Do NOT post a text reply ("принято", "резолвлю", "ок"). - Add ONE reaction emoji (👍 / 💯 / 🚀 — any single expressive reaction) to the author's last note in the thread. - Resolve the thread silently: `{"discussionId":"…","resolve":true}` (no body).
When agreeing with a peer: - 💯 reaction only — no resolve, no text. The thread's OWNER verifies and closes it (see <ThreadModel> rule 1); my agreement is acknowledgement, not closure.
This keeps the MR clean: reaction = acknowledgement, resolve = closure by the owner. No noise.

PostingRules.ThreadModel:
A thread is not "something to react to" — it is a goal someone set. This model gives every thread an owner, a goal, and a next actor, so the agent acts like a considerate co-reviewer: closes only what it owns, judges closure by the goal, and never nags an author who is simply working through replies in order.
Before ANY thread action, annotate every thread: | Field | Values | How determined | |---|---|---| | `owner` | mine / peer / author | author of the thread's FIRST note vs `my_login` | | `goal` | fix-code / answer-question / record-decision / fyi | reconstructed from the first note's text | | `nextActor` | me / author / peer | whom the last substantive note addresses | | `status` | goal-met / waiting-author / waiting-me / stalled | goal vs current diff + replies |
1. **RESOLVE_OWNERSHIP** — resolve only `owner: mine` threads. Exception: I am the MR author — threads on my own MR may be resolved by me when their goal is met. A peer's correct finding → 💯 reaction, NO resolve — the owner verifies and closes. My thread duplicating a peer's → resolve MINE, 💯 theirs. 2. **GOAL_DRIVEN_CLOSE** — my thread closes when ITS goal is met, never because the conversation went quiet: fix-code → the fix is visible in the current diff (re-verify, then 👍 + silent resolve); answer-question → a substantive answer arrived; record-decision → the decision is stated in the thread. Goal not met and author silent → see rule 3, not resolve. 3. **PING_POLICY** — never automatic. Partial replies are not forgetting: authors answer in batches and in order. A «напомнить» candidate exists ONLY when: (a) the author was active in the MR after my thread (pushed commits / replied to other threads) at least TWICE while my thread stayed unanswered, OR (b) my thread blocks approve and everything else is closed. Ping text is neutral («актуально ли ещё?» — never «вы забыли»), goes through the operator's Ask, never posted autonomously. 4. **PARTIAL_REPLY_DEFAULT** — author answered some threads and skipped mine → skipped threads get `status: waiting-author`, action = NONE. Report line for the operator: «ждут автора: N (активен, идёт по порядку — не пинговать)».

ReactionMatrix.Mission: Authority for role × situation → reaction (what action to take). Existing posting rules (PreFlight, AX_POSTING_SILENT_RESOLVE, CommentFormat) govern HOW each action is formatted and posted — this matrix governs WHICH action to take. Per NFC-01: SHA already in repo — agent does not commit.
ReactionMatrix.Matrix: | Role | Situation | Action | |---|---|---| | reviewer | fixed-in-code (my thread) | 👍 + resolve (check diff: file/line in changeset → re-verify; ThreadModel rule 2) | | reviewer | not-fixed (my thread) | reply/repeat; author silent → ThreadModel rule 3 (no auto-ping) | | reviewer | peer-said-same | 💯 on peer's thread, NO resolve (owner closes — ThreadModel rule 1); my duplicate thread → resolve MINE | | reviewer | peer-said-different | reply with position | | reviewer | all-fixed-no-new | approve | | author | reviewer-right | 👍 + reply «согласен, уже исправил в <sha>» (SHA already in repo, agent does not commit — NFC-01) | | author | reviewer-wrong | reply | | author | new-reviewer-comments | check, agree/disagree |

DiagramConversion.Goal: Convert the chat report's diagrams (ASCII/widget) to GitLab-native Mermaid for posting.
DiagramConversion.Rules: 1. Keep the SAME diagram TYPE the report chose — the intent→type mapping is owned by `ai/directives/agent-inbox/visual-vocabulary.directive.xml` ``; load it and convert to that row's Mermaid keyword (tree stays plain text; C4/dependencies → `flowchart`; runtime flow → `sequenceDiagram`; lifecycle → `stateDiagram-v2`; risk-matrix → `quadrantChart`; schema → `erDiagram`). Do NOT collapse everything into a flowchart. 2. Minimal syntax per type — see visual-vocabulary `` (Mermaid column). 3. Keep ≤7 nodes per diagram (arch-interrogation AX_VISUALIZE_WHEN_RELATIONAL / visual-vocabulary AX_DIAGRAM_DISCIPLINE). 4. Use fixed classDef for entity state — COPY AS-IS: - new → green fill (#dafbe1), green stroke (#2da44e) - modified → yellow fill (#fff8c5), yellow stroke (#bf8700) - deleted → red fill (#ffebe9), red stroke (#cf222e) - related/outside MR → gray fill (#f6f8fa), gray dashed stroke (#999) 5. Solid edges for in-change connections, dashed edges for outside-MR connections. 6. Every diagram gets a one-line caption in Russian.

PostingRules.Axiom: Per `AX_INFOGRAPHIC_FIRST` (visual-vocabulary) applied to POSTED comments — not just the overview: when a line-comment or thread-reply explains something RELATIONAL and it fits ≤5 nodes (a flow the author must trace, a dependency they missed, a state transition), embed a small Mermaid diagram instead of a paragraph. A single-point remark stays prose. A wall of diagrams in a thread erodes author trust as much as a wall of text — gate on relational + ≤5 nodes.

CommentFormat.Section:
A standalone discussion (new thread, not tied to a code line). JSON shape:
```json {"body": "🤖 …content with Mermaid diagrams…"} ```

A reply inside an existing discussion thread. JSON shape:
```json {"discussionId": "<full GitLab discussion ID>", "body": "🤖 …reply content…"} ```

A comment attached to a specific code line in the diff. JSON shape:
```json { "body": "🤖 …comment…", "position": { "baseSha": "<base_sha>", "startSha": "<start_sha>", "headSha": "<head_sha>", "newPath": "<file_path>", "newLine": <line_number> } } ```
Line rules (per arch-interrogation diff_refs from vcs-worktree): - added line → `newLine` - removed line → `oldLine` - context line → BOTH `oldLine` and `newLine` - `oldPath` = `newPath` unless file was renamed.

An exact mechanical fix the author applies with one click (Apply suggestion). GitLab syntax: a fenced block ```suggestion:-M+N where M and N are NUMBERS — how many lines above (M) and below (N) the commented line the replacement covers. Single-line replacement → ```suggestion:-0+0. Always write the numeric :-M+N header — vcs-reply validation rejects a bare ```suggestion. INSIDE the block — the full new text of the covered lines (not a diff, not a description). Posted as a line-comment on the target line. JSON shape:
```json { "body": "🤖 Опечатка: `REDDIS_URL` → `REDIS_URL`

```suggestion:-0+0
throw new Error(`REDIS_URL is not set`);
```", "position": { "baseSha": "<base_sha>", "startSha": "<start_sha>", "headSha": "<head_sha>", "newPath": "<file_path>", "newLine": <line_number> } } ```

PostingRules.CandidateTagging: Each candidate from arch-interrogation OutputFormat §9 carries a `kind`: | kind | Meaning | Posting action | |---|---|---| | `new-line-comment` | New finding, not raised before | Post as line-comment on the relevant code line | | `reply-to-thread` | Already raised by another reviewer; I add substance | Post as reply-to-thread with the given discussionId | | `correction-reply` | Another reviewer's claim is wrong per AX_GROUNDED_IN_REPO | Post as reply-to-thread with correction | | `awaiting-my-reply` | Thread where @my_login is mentioned or my last message got a reply | Post as reply-to-thread; operator sees this separately in the report | | `suggestion` | TYPO probe found a typo or style issue | Post as line-comment with ```suggestion:-0+0 fenced block containing new text (see §suggestion) |

VcsReplySyntax.Command: # Post live — the operator's checkbox approval in the skill's action menu IS the # confirmation, so we post directly. No dry-run step in the flow (the `--dry-run` # flag still exists in the CLI for manual debugging, but the skill does not use it). npx tsx ~/Developer/gennady/cli/gennady.ts vcs-reply --url=<webUrl> < comments.json
VcsReplySyntax.Requirement: host from --vcs-host; project and iid from the MR ref (group/project!iid).

PostingRules.HaltConditions: | ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_TOKEN` | GITLAB_PERSONAL_TOKEN not set | | `H_NO_CANDIDATES` | No comment candidates to post (all dropped by dedup or operator skip) |
